customer.name: Harbourline Mutual
customer.summary: Small general insurer (home and motor) seeking same‑day claim triage, reduced document request cycles, explainable decisions, and compliance with regulator constraints, to be live by October.

requirements.statement: Perform first‑touch claim triage (classification and assignment) within the same business day for most claims.

evidence.quote: I want that to be same day.

requirements.statement: Automatically request missing documents and keep the rate of second‑request cycles below ten percent of claims.

evidence.quote: fewer than ten percent needing a second request for documents.

requirements.statement: All automated decision logic must be fully explainable to regulators; no black‑box models may be used.

evidence.quote: every decision has to be explainable to the regulator, so no black box

requirements.statement: Claims with a payout amount over $5,000 must be reviewed and signed off by a human adjuster before closure.

evidence.quote: any claim over five thousand dollars must be signed off by a human adjuster

requirements.statement: Exchange data with the legacy policy system exclusively via nightly SFTP file export/import; no direct API calls.

evidence.quote: It does a nightly file export and import over SFTP, and that's it.
So whatever we build exchanges files with it.

requirements.statement: Phase 1 scope is limited to triage and missing‑document request functionality; fraud scoring is excluded.

evidence.quote: I’d keep fraud out of the first release.

requirements.statement: Deploy the Phase 1 solution no later than October to be ready for storm season.

evidence.quote: Before storm season, so by October.

requirements.statement: Customer data may not be sent to any external party for model training without a completed legal review.

evidence.quote: we can't send customer data to an outside party for training without legal review

requirements.statement: A customer chat assistant is not to be included in Phase 1.

evidence.quote: Please, no. Not until we've done triage properly.

requirements.statement: The solution must avoid any regulatory findings during operation.

stakeholders.name: Dana
stakeholders.concern: Speed of triage and reduction of document request cycles.

stakeholders.name: Imran
stakeholders.concern: Regulatory explainability, human sign‑off thresholds, and data‑privacy.

fewer than ten percent needing a second request for documents

open_questions.question: What percentage of claims qualifies as "most" for the same‑day triage success metric?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Needed to set a measurable target and evaluate system performance.

open_questions.question: What level of explainability (e.g., audit trail, rule traceability) is required for regulator approval?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Ensures the solution meets the "no black box" constraint.

open_questions.question: What is the formal legal review process for any external data usage or model training?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Prevents violation of data‑privacy policies and regulatory penalties.

open_questions.question: What file format and schema will the nightly SFTP export/import use?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Critical for designing the integration layer.

open_questions.question: How will the human adjuster sign‑off for claims > $5,000 be operationalized in the workflow?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Ensures the system can enforce the mandatory human review rule.

risks.risk: Regulatory non‑compliance if decision logic is not fully explainable.
Missing the October go‑live deadline for triage functionality.
Integration challenges with a 15‑year‑old policy system that only supports nightly SFTP.
Potential data‑privacy breach if external training data is used without proper legal clearance.

assumptions: The existing policy system can accept and produce files via SFTP on a nightly schedule without additional development.
The definition of "most claims" for same-day triage is at least 80% of incoming claims.
Human adjuster sign‑off workflow can be integrated into the new system without changing the legacy system.

components.name: SFTP Ingestion Service
components.responsibility: Pull nightly export files from legacy policy system via SFTP, parse and load claim and policy data into internal database.
components.tech: Python script scheduled with cron or managed scheduler, storing data in PostgreSQL
components.size_rationale: Simple scheduled file fetch and CSV parsing; 2‑4 days.

components.name: Claim Intake API
components.responsibility: Accept new claim submissions (web or email attachment), validate, and persist initial claim record.
components.size_rationale: REST endpoint with basic validation; 2‑4 days.

components.name: Rule‑Based Triage Engine
components.responsibility: Classify incoming claims and assign to appropriate adjuster queue using explainable decision tables.
components.size_rationale: Implement decision tables (e.g., Drools) and integrate with claim DB; 5‑10 days.

components.name: Missing Document Automation Service
components.responsibility: Detect missing required documents, generate templated email requests, track responses, and trigger second‑request if needed.
components.tech: Managed workflow tool (e.g., n8n) with SMTP connector
components.size_rationale: Workflow with email templating and state tracking; 5‑10 days.

components.name: High‑Payout Human Sign‑off UI
components.responsibility: Present claims > $5,000 to a senior adjuster for review and digital signature before closure.
components.tech: React front‑end + Node.js backend, storing approvals in PostgreSQL
components.size_rationale: Simple web UI with audit logging; 5‑10 days.

components.name: Audit & Compliance Logging Service
components.responsibility: Record every decision, rule evaluation, document request, and human sign‑off with immutable timestamps for regulator review.
components.tech: Managed ELK stack (Elasticsearch, Logstash, Kibana) with API ingestion
components.size_rationale: Managed logging platform (e.g., Elastic Cloud) with minimal configuration; 2‑4 days.

components.name: Operations Dashboard
components.responsibility: Display same‑day triage rate, missing‑document request rate, second‑request rate, and compliance alerts.
components.tech: Grafana connected to PostgreSQL and Elasticsearch
components.size_rationale: Dashboard pulling from PostgreSQL and ELK; 2‑4 days.

components.name: Workflow Orchestration Engine
components.responsibility: Coordinate claim flow: intake → triage → missing‑document check → high‑payout sign‑off → closure, ensuring state persistence and hand‑offs.
components.tech: Managed workflow service with REST connectors
components.size_rationale: Managed BPM/Workflow service (e.g., Camunda Cloud) integration with multiple components; 10‑20 days.

integrations.method: Nightly SFTP pull of CSV/flat‑file exports
integrations.risk: Medium – requires secure key management and file‑format agreement

tradeoffs.alternative: Buy a commercial explainable AI decision service
tradeoffs.reason: Open‑source rule tables guarantee full auditability and avoid vendor lock‑in, aligning with strict regulator explainability requirement.

tradeoffs.alternative: Custom code orchestration for claim flow
tradeoffs.reason: Reduces development effort and provides built‑in state persistence and audit logs, helping meet the October deadline.

tradeoffs.alternative: Store all data on‑prem for maximum control
tradeoffs.reason: Accelerates delivery and leverages built‑in security/compliance features; on‑prem would add infrastructure overhead and delay go‑live.

tradeoffs.alternative: Integrate with a third‑party email platform for document requests
tradeoffs.reason: Low claim volume makes a lightweight SMTP approach sufficient and avoids additional licensing costs.

savings_drivers.name: Claim triage time reduction
savings_drivers.note: Automated rule‑based triage cuts manual review from ~15 min to ~5 min for most claims.

savings_drivers.name: Missing‑document request handling
savings_drivers.note: Automated email generation and tracking reduces manual effort per request.

savings_drivers.name: Second‑request cycle reduction
savings_drivers.note: Lowering second‑request rate from 14% to target 10% saves follow‑up work.

assumptions: Cloud provider not specified; solution will be cloud‑agnostic (e.g., can run on AWS, Azure, GCP, or on‑prem VM).
File format and schema of the nightly SFTP export are unknown; assume CSV or fixed‑width flat file that can be parsed into claim records.
Email delivery mechanism not specified; assume access to an SMTP relay for sending document‑request emails.
Regulatory explainability requirement will be satisfied with rule‑engine audit trails and decision tables; exact audit‑trail format not defined.
Number of internal users (adjusters, triage staff) not provided; sizing assumes a small team (≤20).

driverSourceFixes: Claim triage time reduction: volume assumed -> stated

caveats: Build cost excludes recurring licence or hosting costs for 2 bought or integrated component(s): Audit & Compliance Logging Service, Workflow Orchestration Engine.
Savings count staff time only. The customer's cycle-time goal is not converted into money.
3 of 3 savings drivers rely on assumed numbers.
